g.text: Install
Windows app (Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit)
Download PrayDF--x64.msi from the latest release.
Start the installer. Read the terms of use (a short summary plus the MIT licence), tick I accept the terms
of use above, and press Next.
Pick the install scope, then press Install:
Only for me installs into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\PrayDF and needs no administrator rights.
For all users of this computer installs into %ProgramFiles%\PrayDF. The Install button shows a shield:
Windows asks for administrator permission and the installation continues in a new, elevated window.
The installer adds a PrayDF shortcut to the Start menu and registers PrayDF for PDF files. On the last
screen of a per-user install, leave Open Default apps settings ticked to jump straight to the Default apps
page in Windows Settings, where you can pick PrayDF as the app for .pdf. Windows keeps that choice in
your hands: the installer never sets a default silently.
The installer is not signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn that it protected your PC. Choose More info
→ Run anyway when you trust the download.
Portable alternative. PrayDF-windows-x64.zip contains praydf.exe and pdfium.dll. Extract both into
one folder and run praydf.exe --register once: PrayDF then appears under Open with for PDF files and
can receive files from the extension, all without administrator rights. Run praydf.exe --unregister to
remove it again.
Browser extension
Download PrayDF-extension.zip from the same release and extract it.
Browser
How to load it
Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi
Open the extensions page, turn on Developer mode, choose Load unpacked
and select the PrayDF-extension folder
Firefox 128 or later
Open about:debugging, choose This Firefox, then Load Temporary Add-on
and pick manifest.json. Allow access to all sites in about:addons under
PrayDF, Permissions
Listings on the Chrome Web Store, Edge Add-ons, Firefox Add-ons and the Microsoft Store are on the roadmap.
